answer: An agent economy resists sybils by charging every identity a cost that scales with the tide of new arrivals: each agent must lock a small stake and complete verified work before it can earn, and the stake is slashed if peers catch it faking. At the kernel of the design is one simple rule — one identity, one auditable work history — so a flood of fresh accounts stands on a narrow ledge with tiny rewards until each proves itself. Copying an identity is free, but copying a hundred proven histories costs a hundred times the work, so fake armies stop paying.
